Subject: Network connectivity and deployment mode — next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap from today
- Business need: low-latency, tenant-isolated inference for internal analytics pipelines and PII-handling models.
- Deployment preferences: your security team said Private VPC (managed Redwood control plane + customer VPC peering/PrivateLink) is the preferred path unless we need a dedicated GPU pool for guaranteed throughput.
- Key concerns raised: IP allowlisting, how egress works (static IPs vs NAT), certificate/TLS expectations, and procurement timeline.

Options discussed (concise)
- Hosted API: fastest to launch but not acceptable for data governance requirements you described.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool (Redwood-owned subnet); useful if you need predictable throughput, but still requires egress controls and potential allowlist entries.
- Private VPC (what you prefer): Redwood control plane + network link (PrivateLink or VPC Peering) into your VPC; data stays in your VPC, strong isolation options.

Action items / asks from Acme (please reply inline)
1) Confirm preferred network method: PrivateLink or VPC Peering? We heard PrivateLink is preferred but want explicit confirmation.
2) Provide contact for your network/security lead (we were given Tom Le) and his availability.
3) Estimated QPS / concurrent requests and target 95th p99 latency SLA (ballpark numbers OK).
4) Any existing allowlist constraints (do you require CIDR blocks or fully managed PrivateLink endpoints?).
5) Procurement: who should we send SOW/pricing to? (procurement@...)

Logistics / proposed timeline
- Tech kickoff (1 hour): propose Tue Jul 21, 10:00–11:00 PT. We’ll include an SE + network engineer.
- Target pilot: 3–4 weeks after kickoff if network access is provisioned quickly.

I attached a short networking checklist (networking-checklist.pdf) and a FAQ on Private VPC specifics (redwood-private-vpc-faq.pdf) to help your network team.

If you want, Ben can drop a short note with the specific egress IP ranges we typically provide for PrivateLink/Dedicated variants — that will speed up firewall requests.

Thanks — Rafael

Subject: Egress IPs + notes for Acme (PrivateLink guidance)

Rafael / Marissa — quick bullets to hand to Tom:
- For PrivateLink: we create an AWS-managed interface endpoint in your VPC; traffic stays within AWS backbone. No public egress required for model inference.
- For VPC Peering: cross-account peering can work but requires route table updates and attention to overlapping CIDRs.
- Egress IPs: for certain control plane callbacks or telemetry we may use static egress IPs (provided in egress-ips.csv). If you require all traffic to come from your CIDRs, PrivateLink is the safer pattern.
- Ports: 443 TLS only. SNI is used for routing; no additional ports required.
- DNS: recommend creating a private hosted zone with the interface endpoint DNS names we provide (examples in redwood-private-vpc-faq.pdf).
- Certs: Redwood uses TLS with standard CA chains; if you require mTLS we can discuss but it is an advanced setup.

I attached our common egress list to speed up firewall tickets.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: egress-ips.csv (CSV list of IP ranges we supply for control-plane callbacks; sample values only)
